newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Commerce Department to investigate fund-raiser.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Commerce Department to investigate fund-raiser.

text.p: The U.S. Commerce Department said on Tuesday it had new questions about Democratic Party fund-raiser John Huang, and it asked its inspector general to investigate.
Meanwhile, Democratic National Committee Chairman Donald Fowler said at a news conference he had set up procedures to prevent future fund-raising errors.
The Democrats say Huang raised $2.5 million for them and that $762,000 raised by him and others has been returned as illegal or inappropriate.
Before he worked at the DNC, Huang was a Commerce Department official.

"The Department of Commerce has referred to its Office of Inspector General records it has retrieved which appear to present questions concerning the conduct of former employee John Huang during his tenure at the department," the department said in a statement. "All documents which may be relevant have been turned over to the Office of Inspector General."
A spokeswoman for the Commerce Department refused to elaborate except to note that the questions arose during research in response to inquiries under the Freedom of Information Act.

Huang, who is at the centre of a political fund-raising controversy, once worked for the Lippo Group, a multibillion-dollar, international firm owned by the Riady family of Indonesia. Huang headed its U.S. subsidiary until he left in 1994 to become a deputy assistant secretary of commerce, a post he held until 1995.

Four contributions he solicited for the DNC have already been returned, including $250,000 from a South Korean company. A Democratic spokeswoman said the money was raised in violation of a federal law prohibiting contributions from foreign companies.
The Democrats also returned $325,000 donated by a man identified as Yogesh Gandhi, the Demcoratic spokeswoman said, because they "could not identify the source of his funds."
Huang travelled to Taiwan to raise funds for the Democrats. Fowler said no other fund-raisers made similar trips, "though we are still checking."
Asked about dozens of visits by Huang to the White House, Fowler said they had been for the purpose of overall planning involved with his job in fund-raising.
Fowler announced a new review process that he said would halt illegal donations. He said the system would ensure "positive, affirmative compliance with all legislative and regulatory requirements."

Fowler defended the committee's record, saying of more than 1 million contributions totalling more than $120 million this year, only 10 checks had been returned so far. It was those checks that totalled $762,00. Democrats are looking at other contributions, Fowler said.
Asked if the controversies surrounding Democratic fund-raising had cost his party control of the House of Representatives in the last election, Fowler said, "It didn't help."
